parsed.refutation_attempt: The variable activationCooldown is an internal simulation timer, set to the constant value 1.0 on line 62 and reset to 1.0 on line 88. It is never derived from any external input (stdin, file, network, argv, environment variables, IPC, or public API parameter). Therefore it does not constitute untrusted data and cannot be considered a credential. The sink on line 111 simply decrements this internal counter by a derived value (1.0 / ticksPerSecond), which is a benign arithmetic operation. No security-sensitive operation is performed with activationCooldown, and the code has no path from external input to a dangerous use of this variable. Hence the claim of a hard‑coded credential vulnerability is unfounded.
